messages:
incident_bot: Pager: dedicated-pool-saturation alert triggered for pool 'eu-west-3-gpu-dedicated-42' — p99 latency > 3s for 5m, queue_depth=142, warmup_inflight=38. Severity: SEV2. https://internal.metrics/redwood/pool/42 :rotating_alert:

incident_bot: Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-pool-saturation — paging on-call.

sara_oncall: I'm on it. jumping in — starting triage. Who's closest to eu-west infra? @mike_sre?

mike_sre: oncall here, looking. grabbing recent grafana snapshot. p95=780ms, p99=3.4s, streaming stalls spiking at tail (stream-end hangs).

julia_prod: seeing customer impact reports — 2 customers with degraded streaming sessions, some partial tokens delivered then stall. CS pinged them.

sara_oncall: ok, top hypothesis: autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough; warmup queue is building and causing head-of-line blocking for streaming connections. queue_depth=142 is higher than our burst threshold of 100.

mike_sre: checking autoscaler logs: scaler requested 4 nodes 4m ago, cloud provider reports "provisioning" delays, one node failed init due to image pull timeout. warmup tasks stuck ~30s each, handshake queueing increased.

ops_lead: can we open temporary override to reserve burst capacity? I can authorize a one-time manual scale to +6 GPUs in that pool. That should reduce queue backpressure while we fix the init failure.

sara_oncall: please do it. Meanwhile I'll toggle route fallback to non-streaming endpoints for affected customers to reduce stall sensitivity.

mike_sre: creating manual scale override now: `rb scale pool eu-west-3-gpu-dedicated-42 --add 6 --duration 20m --reason "hotburst mitigation"`

incident_bot: Command accepted. Manual scale started. Provisioning 6 instances (async). Expected warmup complete ~2-4 minutes after nodes are Ready.

julia_prod: notify customers: "We've detected increased latency and streaming stalls due to a capacity surge. We're adding temporary capacity and will rollback when stable. No model rollback required." Draft posted to status channel.

kevin_support: Customers A and B acknowledged. One requested ETA; gave them 15m.

sara_oncall: good. while we wait, can we reduce streaming session affinity on that pool? even partial responses are valuable. set streaming_timeout to 90s and enable chunked fallback where possible.

mike_sre: toggling server-side streaming gating: `rb feature-flag set pool.streaming_gate.eu-west-3 false` — this will make SDK fall back to poll responses. Applying now.

incident_bot: Feature flag update applied. SDKs will receive non-streaming flows for new sessions. Existing sessions remain.

mike_sre: also noticed kv-cache miss rate jumped 67% — cold KV causing repeated expensive compute on tokens which magnifies tail. We should prime high-frequency prefixes for affected models.

julia_prod: priming started for top 50 prefixes per customer (scripts running). Should reduce per-token cost and marginal latency for follow-on requests.

sara_oncall: any signs of wider region issues? autoscaler image pull error looked transient from provider registry. Opening a provider incident with infra.

ops_lead: provider responded: one init failure due to transient registry throttling, they cleared it; new nodes started provisioning. Expect nodes Ready in ~90s.

mike_sre: new nodes becoming Ready. warmup jobs active. warmup_inflight dropping from 38 -> 12. queue_depth falling to 48. p99 trending down to 1.2s.

julia_prod: updating status page: "Partial degradation — streaming impacted; mitigation in progress." Added note about burst capacity being added.

kevin_support: customers report improved behavior on new sessions. One customer still saw sticky stall on an older connection; advised reconnect.

sara_oncall: reconnects helped?

kevin_support: yes, after reconnect backlog cleared for that tenant.

mike_sre: running post-mortem checklist: collect logs from warmup workers, autoscaler request traces, provider init events, and streaming proxy logs for the 5m window.

incident_bot: Attachments saved to incident artifact: s3://incidents/2601234567/artifacts.tar.gz

ops_lead: once stable, we should revert manual scale and re-enable streaming gating. Plan: rollback scale in 15m, re-enable streaming gate after verification.

sara_oncall: agree. set rollback timer for 20m from now. I'll continue monitoring p95/p99 and queue.

mike_sre: quick notes: root cause = provider-side image registry throttling + insufficient autoscaler retry/backoff for hotshot bursts. Contributing factor = high kv-cache coldmiss during a customer-driven burst which increased per-request compute. Follow-ups: improve autoscaler retry logic, add preflight for pool image pulls, surface warmup queue depth alert earlier (lower threshold), add KV priming on model rollout.

julia_prod: capturing action items in incident ticket and scheduling for next sprint. Assigning to infra and runtime teams.

sara_oncall: marking incident as mitigated. continuing 30m watch. If p99 < 1s and queue_depth < 20 for 10m, we'll close. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident_bot: Incident state changed: MITIGATED by sara_oncall at 2601234620. Duration: 53m.
